item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption examines governance challenges in local Aboriginal land councils and how accountability and regulation could be improved.
item.support: This report examines those challenges and the factors contributing to them.

item.text: It considers member participation, board capacity, conflicts of interest and oversight by the NSW Aboriginal Land Council and the Registrar.
item.support: Member participation rates at meetings in many LALCs are low

item.text: The Commission identifies low participation, limits to board training and overlapping regulatory functions as barriers to effective accountability.
item.support: there is an overlap between regulators such as NSWALC and the Registrar

item.text: The Commission makes 11 improvement suggestions covering member engagement, governance rules, board skills, regulatory coordination, resources and oversight of council entities.
item.support: The following suggestions for improvement are made in this report.

item.quote: There is scope to strengthen the effectiveness of both the Registrar and NSWALC in overseeing LALCs.
There is potential to strengthen members’ ability to hold the leadership of LALCs accountable.
